title: Paper call: Bajaj Finance consolidated AUM growth YoY at 31-Mar-2027 is ≥26.0%
body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.60 (naive base rate 0.55) that: Bajaj Finance consolidated AUM growth YoY at 31-Mar-2027 is ≥26.0%. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (19-Oct-2026): AUM +26.5% YoY to ₹5,84,624 cr; net AUM add ~₹38k cr/qtr for two quarters. CEO Rajeev Jain: 'probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis'; medium-term guide stays 20–25%. Headwinds named: RBI hikes ('baking in two more increases… 6% kind of rates'), NIM compression slightly worse than the 10–15 bps guide, gold-loan short-tenor schemes stopped, El Niño (monsoon 87% LPA). Track record: FY25 guide 26–27%, delivered ~26%. Reasoning: BFL has a long record of hitting AUM guidance, and the guide was given with H1 already at 26.5%; but 26% is the bottom of the range and rate hikes plus rural stress lean against H2 acceleration. Slightly above base. Resolution: YES if consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2027 ÷ consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2026 − 1 ≥ 26.0% (both as stated in BFL's Q4 FY27 results press release/investor deck; use BFL's own reported YoY if it states one). Source: Bajaj Finance Q4 FY27 results press release / investor presentation (NSE announcements). Resolve by 2027-05-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.resolution_source: Bajaj Finance Q4 FY27 results press release / investor presentation (NSE announcements)

title: Paper call: Infosys raises the midpoint of its FY27 constant-currency revenue guidance above 1.5% at Q3 FY27 results
body: Forward test of the base rate method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.70) that: Infosys raises the midpoint of its FY27 constant-currency revenue guidance above 1.5% at Q3 FY27 results. Evidence: Q2 FY27 (Oct-2026): FY27 cc guidance cut from 1.5–3% to 1–2%; op-margin guide 20–22% kept (Q2 ~21%). Q2 cc growth +1.5% YoY, +1.2% QoQ; H1 +1.9% cc. Mgmt cites soft volumes, pricing pressure/AI deflation, weak Retail/Hi-Tech, rate rises; large deals TCV $8.8 bn. Infosys history at Q3: midpoint raised in FY23, FY25 and FY26, unchanged (narrowed) in FY24. Reasoning: H1 at 1.9% means the 1–2% band already embeds a weak H2; Q3 has furloughs, and they just cut. A narrow-upward revision (e.g., 1.5–2%) is plausible but so is a hold. Below the historical base because this year's direction of revision was down. Resolution: YES if the FY27 cc revenue guidance announced with Q3 FY27 results has a midpoint strictly greater than 1.5% (e.g., 1.5–2.0% or 1.75–2.25%). Hold at 1–2% or any cut = NO. Source: Infosys Q3 FY27 press release / fact sheet (infosys.com, NSE). Resolve by 2027-01-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

title: Paper call: Lupin Q3 FY27 company-reported EBITDA margin (ex-forex & other income) is ≥24.0%

Probability 0.35 (naive base rate 0.60) that: Lupin Q3 FY27 company-reported EBITDA margin (ex-forex & other income) is ≥24.0%. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): Q2 EBITDA ex-forex/other income ₹1,957 cr, margin 25.1% vs 31.3% a year ago; FY27 margin guide 'around 24–25%' with CEO Vinita Gupta saying margins 'likely to moderate in the coming quarters' (US competition in key products, R&D ~8% of sales, input costs). We weight management's downbeat tone over persistence. Resolution: YES if the EBITDA margin excluding forex and other income for Q3 FY27, as stated in Lupin's Q3 press release/call, is ≥24.0%. If not stated, compute (EBITDA − other income − forex gain) ÷ revenue from operations from the results. Source: Lupin Q3 FY27 results press release / earnings call transcript. title: Paper call: Transrail Lighting FY27 order intake is ≥₹10,000 cr

'Since listing, we have not missed any of our revenue or margin guidance' (revenue Q2 ₹2,056 cr, +32%; EBITDA margin 11.6%). body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell).
